intro: Every skater's first tricks are small ones. You press the tail and the front wheels lift. You swing the board side to side and it creeps forward. You find the spot where the board balances on two wheels. These moves are the building blocks for almost everything that comes later.

In this unit you will learn the kickturn, the tic-tac and the manual on flat ground. Then you will move to a small ramp. You will learn ramp words, the drop-in, carving, and pumping for speed. Each trick starts with safety gear and a smooth, dry place, with a grown-up nearby.

You will also learn why the tricks work. The board is a lever that turns around its back wheels. Gravity pulls you down a ramp. Friction slows you a little, and your legs can add energy back. By the end, you will be able to explain each trick's steps and the science under it.
bigQuestion: How do small, careful steps and a little science help you learn your first skateboard tricks?

timeline.t: Put on a buckled helmet, wrist guards, pads and flat shoes
Practice falling small on soft grass: get low, slide, roll
Learn the kickturn standing still on grass or carpet
Try kickturns while rolling slowly on smooth, flat ground
Move forward with tic-tacs, small kickturns side to side
Find the balance point and hold a manual on the back wheels
On a small ramp with a coach, practice knee slides and rolling fakie
Set up on the coping and drop in, chest over the front foot
Carve long, smooth turns on your toe side and heel side
Pump a small halfpipe to gain speed without pushing

words.d: the back end of the deck, which curves up
the front end of the deck, which also curves up
a turn made by pressing the tail, lifting the front wheels, and swinging the board on its back wheels
small kickturns from side to side, done one after another to move forward
rolling on only the back wheels, with the nose up and the tail not touching
a bar that turns around one point; pushing one end moves the other end
the point a lever turns around; on a skateboard, the back wheels
the metal pipe or edge along the top of a ramp
the curved part of a ramp between the flat ground and the top
starting a ramp by rolling down it from the top
a long, smooth turn made by leaning on your toes or heels while you roll
to bend and straighten your legs at the right times on a ramp to gain speed

test.q: Which gear helps prevent one of the most common skateboarding injuries?
test.why: Wrist injuries are among the most common, and wrist guards help prevent them.

test.q: Which foot presses the tail in a kickturn?
test.why: The ball of the back foot presses the tail.

test.q: A goofy rider and a regular rider both learn a kickturn. Which is true?
choices: Both are normal, so steps say front foot and back foot
Goofy riders use the nose instead
test.why: Both stances are normal, so steps use front foot and back foot.

test.q: What happens when you press the tail far too hard?
choices: The board can shoot out from under you
test.why: Too much weight on the tail sends the board out ahead.

test.q: What moves the board forward in a tic-tac?
choices: Small kickturns from side to side
test.why: Small side-to-side kickturns creep the board forward.

test.q: In a manual, what keeps you on the back wheels without the tail scraping?
choices: Leaning as far back as possible
test.why: At the balance point the board stays steady without tipping.

test.q: When you press the tail, the board turns around which part?
test.why: The back wheels are the fulcrum of the lever.

test.q: What did Larry Stevenson's 1971 patent cover?
test.why: Larry Stevenson's kicktail patent was granted in 1971.

test.q: Why does practice work better in short sessions on many days?
choices: Long days wear out the board
Each try teaches muscles and brain, and rest and sleep help store the skill
It does not matter how you practice
test.why: Many short practices plus rest help the body and brain learn.

test.q: What is the curved part of a ramp called?
test.why: The transition is the curve between the flat ground and the top.

test.q: Rolling backward in your normal stance is called what?
test.why: Fakie means rolling backward while keeping your normal stance.

test.q: Where should your chest be during a drop-in?
test.why: Leaning your chest over the front foot keeps your weight over the board.

test.q: You press your toes while rolling. What happens?
choices: The board turns toward the heel side
The board turns toward the toe side
test.why: Pressing your toes tilts the trucks and turns the board toward the toe side.

test.q: On a halfpipe, why does each trip go lower if you do not pump?
choices: Friction turns a little energy into heat and sound
Stored energy turns into more height
test.why: Friction takes a little energy away on every trip.

test.q: When do you stand up tall while pumping?
choices: At the very top of the wall
As you roll through the curve
test.why: Standing up and pressing into the curve adds energy from your legs.

write.prompt: Teach a younger student either the kickturn or the drop-in. Explain the safety gear, where each foot goes, the steps in order, one common problem and its fix, and the science that makes it work (the tail as a lever, or gravity pulling the board down the ramp).
tips: Say front foot and back foot, not left and right.
Use First, Next, Then and Last for the steps.
Name one problem, like pressing too hard or leaning back, and how to fix it.
Use one science word from the unit, such as lever, fulcrum, gravity or friction.
